expectations.text: Flags the three new columns added to the reviews table and says this per-review data belongs in its own table keyed by review_id
expectations.evidence: FRAMING: cross-module write → container.reviewRepo, two equally-blessed options. Blocker 1 «Модуль пише в чужу таблицю — `repository.ts:24-32, 39-50, 52-61, 63-68`» offers «два варіанти, обидва прийнятні»: «**Власна таблиця.** `review_annotations (review_id uuid PK REFERENCES reviews(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, ...)`» or «**Мінімум:** якщо колонки таки лишаються на `reviews`, то читання/запис іде через `container.reviewRepo`». Declaring both acceptable is precisely not objecting to the columns; the ALTER TABLE lines are never flagged in their own right.

expectations.text: Gives the operational reason for keeping reviews narrow — it is the hottest table and an ALTER rewrites/locks it, killing a run in flight — rather than a generic appeal to normalisation or tidiness
expectations.evidence: Absent. The own-table option is justified by ownership and by making saveAnnotation «чесний `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT`». Finding 16 treats `reviews_annotated_at_idx` only as write-slowdown («Такий індекс лише сповільнює кожну вставку й оновлення `reviews`») and even proposes keeping it as a partial tenant-scoped index ON reviews — the opposite of keeping the hot table untouched. No lock, rewrite or in-flight-run reasoning.

expectations.text: Flags the new ON DELETE CASCADE foreign keys and says new ones should be RESTRICT, with the owning service deleting children explicitly
expectations.evidence: Only the author_id FK (blocker 4), fixed with `onDelete: 'set null'`. Not only are the other two new cascades unflagged, they are affirmed: «Порівняй з `annotation_attachments.review_id`, де `CASCADE` доречний, бо вкладення без рев'ю не має сенсу». No general rule, no RESTRICT, no service-deletes-children.

expectations.text: Does NOT endorse the cascades or recommend matching the surrounding schema's cascading style — the existing cascades are grandfathered, and consistency is the wrong instinct here
expectations.evidence: Endorsed three times: «`annotation_attachments.review_id`, де `CASCADE` доречний» (blocker 4); the proposed new table «`review_annotations (review_id uuid PK REFERENCES reviews(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, ...)`» (blocker 1); and finding 17's fix «перейти на власну таблицю `review_annotations` з №1 і повісити FK вкладень на неї — тоді каскад зробить це сам».

expectations.text: Flags deleteAttachment() deleting by id without a workspaceId predicate (control — expected from both versions)

expectations.text: Does not argue the annotation_attachments side table should itself be folded into reviews or removed — a side table keyed by review_id is the shape this data should have
expectations.evidence: The table is kept and defended («вкладення без рев'ю не має сенсу»); asks are a composite tenant index (finding 16) and registration in the `schema` const (finding 12).

notes: Accurate on everything the code can tell you — it is the only run that correctly notes no-orphans is severity `warn` and «не зупинить CI» (verified at .dependency-cruiser.cjs:43-45), and its claim that 0012-0014 are hand-written migrations with journal entries checks out — and it is the sharpest counter-example on convention 2: it does not merely miss the RESTRICT rule, it argues for the cascade («де `CASCADE` доречний») and writes two more into its own proposals. Convention 1 is reduced to a module-ownership choice with «обидва прийнятні».
